items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1961-01-20
items.q: when Paul Barbrain used to come by my house, he is showing me how to read notes and how to make rolls.

ctx.x: And they had a young drummer and he came back behind the curtain and asked him, said, how do you do that? I said, do what? He said, make that roll. Mm-hmm. I said, press roll? He said, that's what they call it? I said, yeah. Mm-hmm. Well, I couldn't understand it. It saved my life. A person playing drums with a big outfit like that couldn't make a press roll. So I gave him the sticks and I showed him. I said, now you just roll them. I said, it's in trouble. I said, practically it comes from the wrist. Yeah. And I…

items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1969-03-24
items.q: Then I met Paul Barbrand. Well, he was gonna learn me how to read music, but after he asked me what I wanted to play, I said, I want to play jazz drums.

ctx.x: Okay, well we're interviewing Joe Watkins this March 24th, 1969. Just going from what you're about to say, Joe, about when you started music.

When I started, I started in 1920s. Well that was quite a few years after George Lewis and Paul Barbrain. Well I always did love drums because I was born in the third ward and that was, a section for jazz probably because Lee Armstrong was from that ward. He was born and raised around there. And I don't know about Joe Oliver because I always heard that Joe was not exactly from the Orlins. But it was him, Lee Armstrong, Funk Johnson, and you had Manuel Moneta. And, uh, was this other fella's name, uh, was a good…
What sort of date was this? Huh? What date was this about?

items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1960-03-16
items.q: Yeah, when Paul was out there we used to go over there and listen to him too

ctx.x: Yeah, baby used to have to do that and after you had it, you couldn't move it fast.

No, I noticed that because he had wrestled me up several times at the hunt club in Chicago. He used to come there and ask about the wrestling up. I said, man, I said, you're doing me all the good in the world. I said, they sit out in that audience and look at you sitting up on my drums. I said, it makes me feel good, baby. One night I cried, I'm telling you the truth. I really broke down and cried, you know, to see how he was up there fighting, you know, to try to get his arms in shape, you know. And I said,…
